scope: Retire stale, discontinued or superseded catalog identities and replace them with current first-party product identities where a direct successor exists.

accepted.name: Check Point AI Security
accepted.description: Enterprise platform to discover, protect and govern AI interactions across employees, applications and agents, including secure AI usage, input/output protection and agent tool-call controls.
accepted.why: For security teams governing employee AI usage and protecting custom AI applications and autonomous agents from data exposure and unsafe actions.

accepted.name: Content Toolkit
accepted.description: Semrush content workspace for topic research, SEO briefs, AI article generation, content optimization for Google and AI search, and repurposing into social and email formats.
accepted.why: For marketers and SEO teams who want one data-backed workflow from topic discovery and briefing through writing, optimization and publishing.

accepted.name: Hostinger AI Builder
accepted.description: AI website and web-app builder that creates from prompts, URLs, images or PDFs, with manual and agentic modes plus hosting, databases, logins, payments and SEO tools.
accepted.why: For businesses and makers who want to build and host a working website or lightweight web app in one provider without stitching together separate infrastructure.

accepted.name: Lexis+ with Protégé
accepted.description: Legal AI workspace for research, drafting and analysis grounded in LexisNexis legal content, with conversational workflows powered by the Protégé assistant.
accepted.why: For legal professionals who need AI-assisted research and drafting connected to authoritative LexisNexis sources and legal workflows.

accepted.name: Luma App
accepted.description: AI creative workspace with multimodal agents that plan, generate, iterate and refine image, video, audio and other creative assets across shared projects.
accepted.why: For creative teams that need an agent-driven workflow from brief to coordinated assets and polished deliverables without restarting across separate tools.

accepted.name: Manage AI
accepted.description: AI capabilities embedded in Clio Manage that extract deadlines from court documents, surface matter activity, create tasks and calendar events, and prepare billing workflows for review.
accepted.why: For law firms using Clio Manage that want to reduce routine administrative work while keeping legal professionals in control of approvals and outcomes.

accepted.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
accepted.description: Open-source Microsoft SDK for building and orchestrating production AI agents and multi-agent workflows in Python and .NET, with tools, memory, middleware, observability and human-in-the-loop execution. Microsoft recommends it for new projects replacing archived AutoGen.
accepted.why: For developers building production agent systems that need durable workflows, provider flexibility and explicit orchestration, including migration from archived AutoGen.

accepted.name: PlayHT
accepted.description: AI text-to-speech and voice-generation platform with Play3.0-mini and PlayDialog models, voice cloning, multilingual speech generation and low-latency streaming APIs.
accepted.why: For creators and developers who need expressive narration, voice cloning or real-time multilingual speech in apps and media workflows; official documentation continues to describe current models and API endpoints.

accepted.name: Semantic Kernel
accepted.description: Open-source SDK for integrating AI models, plugins, memory and orchestration into .NET and Python applications. It continues to receive releases; Microsoft Agent Framework is a newer agent-focused option, not a notice that Semantic Kernel has been discontinued.
accepted.why: For developers adding model providers, plugins, memory and orchestration to existing .NET/Python applications; Microsoft continues to publish releases while Agent Framework offers a newer agent-focused path.

accepted.name: Superhuman Mail
accepted.description: AI-native email client for Gmail and Outlook with fast inbox triage, writing, search, summaries, reminders and team collaboration.
accepted.why: For high-volume email users and teams who want to triage messages, draft replies and follow up faster.

accepted.name: Tabnine
accepted.description: AI coding assistant for code completion, chat and agentic development workflows, with code review, code explanation, refactoring and enterprise privacy/deployment controls. The product remains active under Tricentis.
accepted.why: For developers and engineering teams that need context-aware coding assistance, agentic workflows and enterprise controls inside supported IDEs; Tabnine's official release notes continue to document active releases.

accepted.name: Topaz Video
accepted.description: Professional AI video enhancement software for upscaling, denoising, sharpening, stabilization, slow motion and frame interpolation on macOS and Windows.
accepted.why: For editors, filmmakers and archivists improving existing footage quality rather than generating entirely new video.

accepted.name: Vibe
accepted.description: Mistral's unified AI agent for professional productivity and coding across web, mobile, terminal and VS Code, supporting multi-step research, drafts, summaries, tool use and software workflows.
accepted.why: For professionals and developers who want one agent for knowledge work and coding, with visible actions and approval controls.

superseded.reason: Microsoft's official repository marks AutoGen archived and no longer maintained. Microsoft says it will provide no bug fixes, security fixes, new features or support, warns against production use, and directs new projects to Microsoft Agent Framework.
Clio's own product and company updates describe Clio Duo's evolution into Manage AI, now embedded in Clio Manage. The active catalog entry uses the current product identity.
Semrush's official FAQ states that ContentShake AI was folded into the main platform and renamed Content Toolkit. The old standalone identity is superseded.

Freepik's official announcement states that Freepik AI became Magnific, with the creative tools and account experience consolidated under Magnific. The active Magnific row already covers the successor.
Hostinger's official changelog states that Horizons and Website Builder became the unified AI Builder product. The old Horizons identity is replaced by Hostinger AI Builder.
Check Point acquired Lakera and now presents the current enterprise offering under Check Point AI Security. The standalone Lakera identity is superseded by the integrated platform.
Mistral's official help center states that Le Chat is now Vibe, with the same account, plan and conversation history. Replace the old product name with Mistral Vibe.
LexisNexis renamed the product Lexis+ with Protégé and describes the current legal AI workspace under that identity. The old Lexis+ AI label is superseded.

Luma's current information identifies Dream Machine as an older deprecated model replaced by Ray, while Luma App is the current consumer creative workspace. Replace the legacy model entry with Luma App.
Superhuman's official product announcement identifies the email client as Superhuman Mail; Superhuman is now the broader suite/company brand. Use the specific active product name.
Topaz's official documentation marks Topaz Video AI as a discontinued legacy application and identifies Topaz Video as the current app with ongoing model updates.

retired.name: Devika
retired.reason: The official repository describes Devika as an early experimental project with many unimplemented or broken features and points to a future second iteration. It does not meet the directory's current usefulness bar.

retired.name: Flowise
retired.reason: Flowise's official sunset notice set end of life for August 31, 2026, with the repository archived in August. It is no longer an active product to recommend.

retired.name: GitHub Spark
retired.reason: GitHub's official deprecation notice ended new Spark app creation and access to existing Spark apps on August 31, 2026. Remove the retired product from the active directory.

retired.name: Sora
retired.reason: OpenAI's official discontinuation notice ended the Sora web and app experience on April 26, 2026 and the API on September 24, 2026. Remove the discontinued product.

mergedIntoExisting.reason: Freepik's official announcement states that Freepik AI became Magnific, with the creative tools and account experience consolidated under Magnific. The active Magnific row already covers the successor.

updatedExisting.name: Magnific
updatedExisting.reason: Updated the existing Magnific entry to reflect the current unified creative platform and the Freepik AI consolidation; confirmed the limited free plan and paid tiers.

updatedExisting.name: Semantic Kernel
updatedExisting.reason: Retained as an active SDK: Microsoft continues publishing Python and .NET releases. Agent Framework provides a newer agent-focused path, but does not make Semantic Kernel discontinued.

recommenderChanges.reason: Current multimodal creative workspace replaces the deprecated Dream Machine product identity.

notes: All replacements and retirements were checked against current first-party product announcements, product pages or official documentation.
Freepik AI is merged into the existing Magnific entry; no duplicate Magnific row is created.
Flowise, GitHub Spark and Sora are removed because their official notices document end-of-life or discontinuation.
Devika is removed because its own repository describes it as an early experimental build with incomplete and broken functionality.
Historical catalog batch files are retained as provenance; active catalog, lifecycle, recommender and release-monitor surfaces are updated.
No popularity, traffic, revenue, ranking or customer-count claims were used as acceptance evidence.

AutoGen is archived and no longer maintained; Microsoft explicitly says it will provide no bug fixes, security fixes, new features or support, warns against production use, and recommends Microsoft Agent Framework for new projects.

Semantic Kernel remains active and is retained: Microsoft's official GitHub releases show ongoing Python and .NET releases, including Python 1.45.0 on 2026-10-06. Agent Framework is a newer agent-focused path, not evidence that Semantic Kernel has been discontinued.

Rechecked two earlier exclusions that had relied on homepage/redirect failures: PlayHT is restored based on its current first-party model/API documentation; Tabnine is restored based on its current product page and active first-party release notes. Neither is classified as discontinued.

rechecked.name: PlayHT
rechecked.reason: First-party documentation remains live and documents current Play3.0-mini and PlayDialog models plus active HTTP/WebSocket APIs. The earlier homepage fetch failure was not evidence of product discontinuation.

rechecked.name: Tabnine
rechecked.reason: The official product page still markets Tabnine as an AI coding assistant acquired by Tricentis, and first-party release notes show active v6.0.0 releases in March 2026 plus current Tabnine Agent documentation. The root-domain redirect was not evidence of product discontinuation.
